PullRequest.Title: Show Copilot Fusion instead of Auto in the model picker at startup
PullRequest.Body:
Before the agent host publishes its models, the chat model picker could show "Auto" with an "Efficiency" readout on startup, then switch to "Copilot Fusion" once models loaded. There were two causes:

- The picker's fallback for an empty selection was hard-coded to "Auto".
- A cached or restored Auto selection kept the name and tier list it was saved with until live metadata arrived.

This change:

- Makes the empty-selection fallback read "Copilot Fusion" in the desktop and phone pickers.
- Hides the stale name and effort readout of a first-party Auto selection that is not yet registered, until live metadata arrives. A live provider-confirmed Auto and user-provided models are shown as before.
- Has a restored conversation model take the model list's current metadata over its saved snapshot.

Model ids, configuration values and routing are unchanged.

## Validation

- `chatInputModelSelectionController.test.ts` (including 3 new restore cases): 60 passed, run in the VS Code test runner.
- New `modelPickerStartup.test.ts`, which renders the desktop and phone pickers: 4 passed, covering empty startup, cached Auto before discovery, the switch to live Fusion metadata, live legacy Auto, and a user-provided model named auto.
- `pnpm run transpile-client`, ESLint on the changed files and the pre-commit hygiene hook (including oxlint) passed.
- A full application cold start was not exercised.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop chat model picker cold startup with no live catalog or a restored legacy Auto snapshot
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Chat input construction renders ModelPickerWidget._renderLabel synchronously before the picker label is usable. The diff adds only isPendingLegacyAutoModel: constant metadata checks plus getVendors/find and getLanguageModelIds/includes; no asynchronous or external operation blocks startup.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The added work is O(V + M) in registered vendors and cached model IDs and allocates two short arrays through existing service accessors, once per label render while the selected model is legacy Auto. Realistic catalogs are small, and non-Auto/Fusion/user-provided selections short-circuit before the ID scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI render; no queue, limiter, IPC, subprocess, filesystem, database, or network concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: With a cold empty language-model cache, getLanguageModelIds returns an empty array and the restored Auto is treated as pending. With a warm/live cache, membership is found in the current in-memory Map keys. No new positive/negative cache or retry behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full helper, service implementations, widget listeners, and render call sites were traced. The only new cost is bounded in-memory array creation and linear membership checks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact catalog sizes and label rerender counts vary by extensions and UI state, but no high-frequency event or expensive boundary reaches this helper; the surrounding render already performs DOM replacement and geometry measurement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The diff changes startup presentation without adding an actionable latency, CPU, GC, or boundary regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Phone chat input startup and reactive mode/model label updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MobileChatInputCombinedPickerActionItem._updateTrigger synchronously clears and rebuilds the compact trigger. The helper is evaluated before text is appended; it performs only in-memory service reads. ILanguageModelsService was already instantiated by ChatInputPart, so the new constructor injection does not activate a new service on this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: For pending legacy Auto only, cost grows linearly with vendor/model catalog size. Autorun frequency is bounded by mode/model changes rather than frames, keystrokes, or scrolling.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous autorun per active phone chip; updates serialize on observable mode/model changes and do not spawn concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The check reads the shared language-model service's existing vendor/model maps. Cold catalog state yields pending Fusion presentation; publication warms the existing model cache and the next model observable update reads it. There is no polling, retry, or retained per-render cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor ownership, ChatInputPart dependencies, autorun triggers, and service registration were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Multiple chat inputs could each own a chip, but only rendered active surfaces react, and the added arrays remain catalog-sized and short-lived.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added dependency and scans do not create eager heavyweight initialization or realistic UI jank.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live model discovery switches restored Auto metadata to Copilot Fusion on desktop and phone
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider publication updates the existing in-memory model cache and emits onDidChangeLanguageModels. Desktop synchronously rerenders its label; phone updates when the selected-model observable changes. The diff adds catalog-membership checks on those renders but no provider resolution or external request.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One added O(V + M) check per affected picker render after a publication/selection update, with effective cardinality equal to rendered picker instances, not model rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing service publication fans out synchronously to listeners; the diff neither increases publication cardinality nor creates parallel boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold restored metadata is distinguished from the warm authoritative model cache. Once the identifier is present, the helper's membership result changes immediately; no stale negative cache or repeated miss-triggered discovery is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the language-model event listener, phone observable path, helper, and service cache access were traced end to end.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous rendered chat inputs is product-state dependent, but the diff performs no per-row model resolution and no remote work for each listener.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Existing event fan-out remains unchanged and the added local work is too small and infrequent to establish a concrete regression.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and all diff pages. Traced desktop and phone startup/render paths, service lifecycle, catalog accessors, publication listeners, cache state, and external-boundary reachability. No reportable performance issue or regression-fix learning signal was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
